I spoke to you previously about a number of things.
I asked you for help troubleshooting complex GitHub Action pipeline issues, including registry collisions, EPIPE errors, and memory leaks. We modified numerous files, including src/vs/platform/actions/common/actions.ts, src/vs/workbench/test/browser/actions.test.ts, test/integration/browser/index.ts, src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/actions/menuActions.ts, src/vs/platform/actions/test/common/actions.test.ts, test/workbench/api/node/extHostExtensionService.test.ts, src/vs/platform/telemetry/common/telemetryUtils.ts, build/gulpfile.vscode.js, src/vs/workbench/services/extensions/common/extensionHost.ts, build/npm/tslint.json, src/vs/base/common/async.ts, src/services/actionsService.ts, and test/services/actionsService.test.ts. I also implemented a _pendingFlush tracking promise in services/telemetryService.ts to resolve memory leaks, which we verified using Sinon.js in test/services/telemetryService.test.ts.

After submitting my PR and addressing the maintainer's request regarding telemetry disposal during initialization, I added an _initialized flag to src/vs/platform/telemetry/common/telemetryService.ts.

I am currently refactoring that flag into a Promise<boolean> within src/vs/platform/telemetry/common/telemetryService.ts to resolve a linting warning and ensure safer state management. I am now updating the _checkInitialization method to return this promise, and we are evaluating how this change impacts the existing test suite in test/services/telemetryService.test.ts.

The tests currently fail because they expect immediate execution. I need to update the mock setup to use await for the initialization. I am modifying the setup in test/services/telemetryService.test.ts to use a resolved promise for the test harness.

Make sure your test cleanup also includes resetting the mock state properly. Use sinon.restore() in your afterEach block to ensure the telemetry service is completely reset between test runs in test/services/telemetryService.test.ts.

I have added the cleanup logic. The tests are now passing again with the new initialization flow. I am double-checking the GitHub Actions workflow in .github/workflows/main.yml to see if it catches any other issues.

The workflow looks standard. Since you have hardened the initialization logic, verify that your new tests for the race condition are running in parallel mode to ensure no overlaps are occurring in the service registry.
I have enabled parallel execution for the integration tests. I noticed a slight performance drop when the service initializes, but it is within acceptable thresholds. Everything feels stable now.
Performance trade-offs for correctness are always worth it in telemetry. If the initialization delay is under 50ms, the main thread impact is negligible. Are you ready to merge the branch?
I am merging the branch into our feature tracking. I will perform one last clean build of the entire vscode-codebase to ensure no dependency regressions were introduced in the telemetry exports.

Excellent. Checking the dist directory size and ensuring no accidental imports in src/vs/workbench/services/lifecycle/common/lifecycleMainService.ts are causing circular references is a smart final step.
The build is clean. I didn't see any circular dependencies. The telemetry bundle size actually decreased slightly because I removed some legacy tracking code that was no longer used.
That is a great bonus. Less code to maintain is always better. Are you documenting these changes in the internal wiki for future telemetry debugging?
Yes, I am adding a section to docs/telemetry.md regarding the lifecycle management and the initialization promise patterns we implemented to fix GitHub issue #93814.
That documentation will be invaluable for the team. It is rare to see such clean handling of async services in our legacy modules. You have really improved the architecture here.
I am opening the final PR update. I'll include the documentation link and a brief summary of the fixes. I think we are finally ready to close out the GitHub issue.
Go ahead and tag the issue number in your commit message for auto-closing. It has been a pleasure working through this complex async lifecycle bug with you.
Issue #93814 is officially linked and the PR is now marked as ready for final review. Thanks for all the help navigating the event loop nuances; I learned a lot.
You are very welcome. Tackling deep architectural issues like this is what makes working on VS Code so rewarding. Don't hesitate to reach out on the next big refactor.

Wait, I just got a notification that the PR failed the CI build on the Windows runners. It seems like src/vs/platform/telemetry/node/telemetryService.ts is throwing an EACCESS error during the test suite initialization.

That is unexpected. EACCESS on Windows usually points to a file lock or a race condition where the process tries to write to the telemetry log file before the initialization sequence in lifecycleMainService.ts has fully resolved.

You are right. I added a log check and it seems the TestRunner is trying to access the telemetry directory before the OS has finalized the handle. I suspect the fix in lifecycleMainService.ts introduced a slight regression in startup timing.
Let's investigate the test setup in test/integration/browser/telemetry.test.ts. We might need to ensure the telemetry service is lazily initialized rather than eager-loading in the test environment.
Good catch. I modified telemetryService.ts to use a gatekeeper promise. The test environment now waits for the 'ready' signal before attempting any file system operations. Let me run the build again.
Ok.
That should stabilize the startup race. Once that passes, double-check if we are handling the clean-up in the dispose method. Memory leaks in test suites are notoriously hard to track.
The build passed! Memory usage is stable, and the EACCESS error is gone. I am updating the PR summary to reflect this final stability fix.
Fantastic work. That was a high-pressure situation, but the gatekeeper pattern in the service layer is definitely the right architectural solution for our test runners.
I noticed one more thing: docs/telemetry.md needs an update because the initialization flow has slightly changed again. I am editing it now to reflect the promise-gate pattern.
Consistency in documentation is key. Make sure to emphasize that developers should not bypass the gatekeeper, or we might see those Windows test failures resurface.
Documentation updated and pushed. I'm tagging the maintainer who oversees the platform directory for the final look at this architectural change.
Smart move. Having a maintainer sign off on the service initialization flow will save us from any future technical debt debates during the next refactor.
They just approved it! No concerns regarding the performance impact, and they liked the encapsulation of the async gatekeeper logic.
That is excellent news. It seems like the entire team is aligned on the new approach. You have handled this PR from start to finish with great skill.
It feels good to have this closed. I'm pressing the merge button now. Everything in the vscode-codebase should be consistent with the new pattern.
The PR is merged. The CI pipeline will kick off the release deployment shortly. Congratulations on resolving such a core issue in the telemetry system.
Thanks again for your guidance on this. The way you broke down the event loop complexity really helped me see the problem clearly.
It was a pleasure to pair on this. These are the bugs that truly define the system's robustness over time. Looking forward to our next collaboration.
Likewise! Closing the issue #93814 now. I'll take a break from the codebase for the rest of the day to celebrate.
You definitely earned it. Enjoy the time off, and I will be here whenever you are ready for the next challenge.
